headline: A White House waiver of the new Graham Act sanctions on Russia pulled Brent down about 1.4 percent to 108 dollars in Monday Asian trade, easing one of the inflation inputs behind a week in which the 10 year Treasury yield held above 5 percent and the Nasdaq lost 4.48 percent.

summary.us: The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.15 percent to 26,140.03 on Friday and the S&P 500 lost 1.09 percent to 7,659.44, as worry shifted from whether AI compute is wanted to who funds it, with CoreWeave bond yields pushed above 15 percent and a Goldman Sachs note reporting the second fastest hedge fund selling of AI stocks in more than a year. For the week the Nasdaq fell 4.48 percent and the S&P 500 about 1.95 percent while the Dow gained 0.67 percent on defensive rotation, after September CPI at 3.7 percent kept a quarter point hike at the October 28 FOMC in play.
summary.india: The Nifty 50 closed 0.65 percent higher at 23,146.15 on Friday and the Sensex added 414 points, with the Nifty IT index up 3.9 percent on the day and 11.7 percent on the week on Q2 earnings from TCS, Tech Mahindra and Wipro. FIIs net bought 1,166 crore rupees on October 16 while DIIs net sold 3,661 crore, against October foreign outflows that trackers put between 44,000 and 52,000 crore rupees, and HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank reported on Saturday with profits up 4.7 percent and 20.1 percent respectively.
summary.global: The Nikkei 225 rebounded 1.39 percent to 65,324.29 on Friday after a 4.9 percent drop on Thursday driven by the US tech rout, while the DAX rose 0.95 percent to 25,622.62 on defence shares and the FTSE 100 led Europe with a 3.13 percent weekly gain. Brent settled at its highest since May 19 on Friday before slipping about 1.4 percent on Monday after the Russia sanctions waiver, and the Bank of Japan is reported to be leaning against a back to back hike at its October 30 meeting.

weekly.narrative: The week belonged to the cost of money rather than the promise of AI. Hot September CPI and PPI prints pushed fed funds futures toward pricing another quarter point increase by year end, and with the 10 year above 5 percent the market stopped asking whether AI compute is wanted and started asking who funds it: CoreWeave credit default swaps hit a record, the iShares Semiconductor ETF fell for eight straight sessions, and the Nasdaq shed 4.48 percent on the week while the Dow, carried by defensives, held a 0.67 percent gain. India went the other way, with the Nifty adding 3.44 percent as IT earnings landed well and the rupee rallied for six sessions on RBI intervention, even as October foreign outflows neared 50,000 crore rupees. Commodities split sharply, with WTI up 7.83 percent on a large US inventory draw and Strait of Hormuz risk while silver dropped 5.83 percent and gold was little changed, and crypto drifted lower on continued spot ETF outflows and close to a billion dollars of leveraged liquidations. Next week brings the 30,213 crore rupee Jio Platforms IPO, the largest in Indian history, alongside Tesla and Netflix earnings, Infosys on Friday and flash PMIs, all inside the Fed blackout that runs to the 28 October decision.
